sentences.span: December, then hold, whereas markets expect nearly four hikes in aggregate.
sentences.why: Multiple sources in the window (this file plus 17247) describe markets pricing several more hikes beyond the first one, supporting the 'not the end, the start' framing as a genuine reading of the tape rather than an invented stance.

sentences.span: whereas markets expect nearly four hikes in aggregate
sentences.why: Continuation of s1's supported thought — more hikes still priced after the first one.

No source states the 10-year at 4.99%. Sources in-window show a range (4.925%, 4.95%, 4.96%, 5.02%, 5.04%, 'crossed 5%') but never this exact print; this is a live-market quote, not a PDF-sourced figure.

sentences.span: Investors quickly connected this trend to an impending wave of demand for advanced processors, networking equipment, cloud hosting, and security APIs, revitalizing the broader tech hardware supply chain.
sentences.why: The 'consumer AI = hardware order' link is genuinely in the sources (this file, plus the UBS and GS memory notes). But 'the part of the AI trade with the fewest people arguing against it' is not stated anywhere, and this same GS note explicitly describes active 'too far, too fast' debate around the AI infrastructure trade — the superlative consensus claim is invented on top of real material.

sentences.span: Apptopia estimated 1.8 million iOS downloads for Muse in the US and Canada, versus 1.3 million for ChatGPT
sentences.why: Exact match to UBS (source field confirmed via 17468.meta.json), including the 13-day window stated a few lines earlier. The Meta +21%/SPX +1% clause is separately confirmed verbatim in JPM's 17526 ('Meta shares up 21% since the launch of Muse 2 weeks ago, vs. the SPX +1%'); no misattribution since that clause carries no bank tag in the pulse sentence.

sentences.span: Samsung HBM4 yields have reportedly reached ~80%, up from below 60% in early mass production
sentences.why: Exact match, Goldman source (gs- file). NAND clause matches 'roughly 20% QoQ pricing upside in both 3Q and 4Q' in the same file — flash is NAND, and 3Q+4Q is fairly rendered as 'a second straight quarter.'

sentences.span: Less than 30% of S&P stocks are now above the 50-day moving average.
sentences.why: Goldman source matches first clause exactly. Second clause ('more 52-week lows than highs for five sessions... near a record') matches 17474__super-ficial-rally.txt verbatim: 'five straight days of more 52wk lows than highs even as the index has rallied back near all-time highs.'

sentences.span: The CCC minus single-B spread has widened to 799bp, close to the top of its available three-year range
sentences.why: Exact figure and range description match.

sentences.span: The six-month ATM implied-volatility spread between IWM and SPX has fallen close to the bottom of its two-year range.
sentences.why: 'Near a two-year low' is a faithful restatement of 'close to the bottom of its two-year range'; 'barely more than the same contracts on the S&P' matches 'small premium to large-cap volatility.'

sentences.span: The average U.S. diesel price hit a new record this week, $6.29 per gallon, up 68% from $3.74 a year ago, according to Energy Information Administration data.
sentences.why: The diesel/EIA figures are exact and faithful. But 'Trump backed an export ban Tuesday evening to cap it' rests on nothing but a bare five-word news-link title in the JPM afternoon briefing ('Trump diesel export ban Ukraine Russia Iran (CNBC)') that establishes no direction, no timing, and no purpose — presenting that as a confirmed policy stance taken at a specific time is asserting far more than the source supports.

sentences.span: The ICE gasoil crack spread has risen to around $95/bbl this week, up from an average of roughly $74/bbl in August.
sentences.why: ING (bylined Ewa Manthey/Warren Patterson, ing.com). The gasoil crack spread is exactly the refining margin the sentence describes in plain English; figures match exactly.

No source states this causal mechanism (that a US export ban is 'the one policy' compressing the crack-spread margin the ING trade depends on). It's a reasoning chain built on top of s10's unsupported export-ban premise, not itself present in any source.

sentences.span: This marks the sixth consecutive year the IAEA has revised its projections higher... ~60% of new nuclear capacity could come from SMRs
sentences.why: 'Carrying most of the new North American capacity' fairly represents the source's ~60% figure.

sentences.span: the US-South Korea nuclear power investment agreement is set to be signed on September 18
sentences.why: Two problems. First, Yuanta's own report only forecasts the signing ('set to be signed'), and no source in the window confirms it actually happened — presenting it as a completed 'signed' deal asserts a conditional as fact. Second, the $96.50/lb 'record' figure is not Yuanta's number (Yuanta's own file states the record as $97/lb); $96.50 comes from a different bank (Northland Capital Markets, file 17438), so tagging the whole sentence '(Yuanta)' misattributes that figure.

sentences.span: uranium prices need to rise to US$120/lb, so as to match supply with demand
sentences.why: Matches Yuanta's stated $120/lb balancing level almost verbatim; the invalidation framing (flat contract cycle disproving it) is a reasonable falsifiable-condition restatement of the same thesis, not an added fact.
